text: The Mysore Palace building is open to visitors every day of the week [1]. Inside the main halls, you will find painted plaster surfaces that are deliberately kept dark for preservation [2]. Additionally, there is a small upstairs museum containing prints, coins, and Tipu's belongings, which include copies of his letters [2].

text: You can try a soft, ghee-heavy dosa from Mylari or a full Andhra meal served on a banana leaf at Hotel RRR [1]. Other local options include a Mysore masala dosa with red chutney spread inside, a plate of idli at a tiffin room, and filter coffee [2]. Additionally, you should try the soft version of Mysore pak, a sweet made of gram flour, ghee, and sugar syrup [2][3].

text: The story goes that the bazaar in front of the temple was once a market street over half a kilometre long where traders sold gems openly by the heap under stone roofs [1]. The colonnades running east from Virupaksha served as the old chariot street, where families lived and traded for generations until they were moved out in 2011 as part of a World Heritage conservation plan [2]. Today, visitors will see empty stone shells that represent a recent heritage decision rather than a ruin from 1565 [2].

text: The famous illumination of the Mysuru Palace takes place on Sunday evenings and public holidays, roughly from seven to eight [1]. During these times, close to a lakh of bulbs come on all at once across the palace for about an hour [1][2][3]. This tradition of lighting the palace on Sundays began after the Maharaja lit it using hydroelectric power in 1905 [4].

The Virupaksha Temple is one of the oldest continuously functioning temples in India, having served as a working shrine before the empire existed, possibly as far back as the seventh century [1][2]. When the city burned in 1565, worship at the temple somehow carried on and has not stopped since [1]. During the fifteenth century, a chieftain named Lakkana Dandesha built the central hall and the fifty-metre-high eastern gateway tower over a far older core shrine [3].

text: When visiting the Virupaksha Temple in Hampi, you should dress with your shoulders and knees covered, just as you would for any working temple [1]. Additionally, wearing a pair of socks is helpful because you must walk barefoot on stone that gets very hot between eleven and four [2].

text: Abbey Falls is a popular waterfall located inside a private coffee estate near Madikeri [1][2]. While the flow of the waterfall is heavy and loud during and just after the monsoon from July to October, the water flow becomes thin by March or April [1][2]. The provided sources do not mention the specific condition of Abbey Falls or whether it is worth visiting in December, so it is best to plan your visit early in the day to avoid the crowds [1].

The shrine of the Chamundeshwari Temple is small, old, and dark, dating back to Hoysala times, while its seven-storeyed gold-topped tower was added later in the eighteenth century [1]. Reading this tower from the bottom up shows a list of gods in order of rank, with smaller attendants at the top [1]. To reach the temple, you can climb a thousand-odd stone steps or take a twenty-minute drive by road [2]. If you choose to climb, you will see numbered steps smeared with vermilion and turmeric by pilgrims [3].
